newsitem.title: CANADA: RTRS-Placer Dome says Suharto involved in Busang vetting.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Placer Dome says Suharto involved in Busang vetting.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto has asked his friend Muhammad "Bob" Hasan to vet proposals for the rich Busang gold find and his advice will likely determine whether bidding is opened up, Placer Dome Inc said Wednesday.

After weeks of intense lobbying in Jakarta, Placer president John Willson said in an interview that he thinks the odds are 50-50 that competitive bidding will be allowed for the right to develop Busang. Barrick Gold Corp has been negotiating a deal with Bre-X Minerals Ltd which discovered the deposit.

"I think in essence the President has asked his lifelong friend Bob Hasan...to look into these companies and make a recommendation," Willson said. Bre-X, Barrick and Hasan's group are in the midst of negotiations, he said.
The Indonesian government in November directed Bre-X to strike a joint venture with Barrick on Busang, which is estimated to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold.

But they have not finalized a deal and Placer last month sought to get its foot in the door by proposing a US$5 billion merger with Calgary-based Bre-X and announcing it would give a 40 percent stake in the deposit to Indonesian interests.
Asked whether he expected Suharto to follow Hasan's recommendation, Willson said, "Yes I do."
But he was not sure whether Hasan would back Placer's plan. "That's not really clear," he said.

Placer previously said that Hasan, a billionaire timber tycoon and Suharto golfing partner, encouraged Placer to make its merger proposal. Indonesia's Nusamba group, 80-percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto and 10 percent by Hasan and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto, has bought 50 percent shareholdings in two companies with minority stakes in two areas of Busang on the island of Borneo.
Willson expected Hasan to make his recommendation to the government by a mid-February deadline previously set for negotiations between Bre-X, Barrick and local partners.

But Barrick may still have the inside track thanks to alliances it forged with Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana, he said. Bre-X, which has lobbied for the right to choose its partner, has a consulting deal with Suharto's eldest son, Harjojudanto.
While Willson expected Hasan's recommendation to be decisive, the final decision "rests in the hands of Mr. Hasan's recommendation, the President and the President's family," he said.
"I don't know how Mr. Hasan's relationship competes with relationships between the President and his family," Willson said. "I can't possibly make any prediction...."

In apparent reference to reports that Barrick was revising its deal to include greater participation for Indonesian investors, Willson said his rival may seek to match Placer's offer. Barrick's plan called for it to get 67.5 percent of Busang, Bre-X 22.5 percent and an Indonesian firm 10 percent.
Willson did not rule out increasing Indonesian participation in Placer's deal beyond 40 percent.
"One would have to look at what is on the table," he said.
